target: Independent positive-event corroboration and observed-mask coverage around Argentine trekking route corridors; not an ignition or advance fire-risk prediction.

protocol.event_source: Official SNMF reported events, deduplicated by date/route/coordinate cluster; 10 km route buffer.
protocol.products: VNP14A1.002, VJ114A1.002, VJ214A1.002 daily 1 km VIIRS fire-mask composites.
protocol.spatial_coordinates: Use the product's XDim/YDim projection-coordinate vectors with its sinusoidal projection and earth radius; nearest grid sample for incident point and full-polyline buffer extraction.
protocol.observed_clear_non_detection: FireMask 5 and QA land/water bits 0-1 equal 10 (land).
protocol.unknown_labels: Mask classes 0-4 and 6, missing tiles, QA coast/water/missing, and incomplete coverage are not converted to negative labels.
protocol.independence: Sensor products for one date/event and multiple report records may observe the same physical event; no precision confidence interval or model score is estimated.

limitations: The event cohort contains reported positives only; it cannot estimate alert precision, specificity, or false-alarm rate.
A daily composite has no exact overpass or ignition time and may include a fire detected before or after the reported start date.
An SNMF coordinate near a route is not proof the fire affected the trail; incident coordinates may be approximate.
Class 5 describes a clear-land non-detection in the composite cell, not proof of no physical fire in the wider route buffer.
Repeated satellite detections and product sensors are not independent physical-fire events.
